sections.title: Ultra Sun Glare Occluded by World Geometry
items: The Ultra veiling glare now draws as background before the world pass, alongside the sun disc: `FramePipeline.render` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/opengl/pipelines/frame.py` and the WGPU render encoder in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/wgpu/runtime/backend.py` issue the `SunPass.draw_glare` and `create_sun_glare_pipeline` draws before the world, and both write no depth so the opaque world drawn next overdraws them. World geometry nearer than the sun therefore occludes the glow at the terrain silhouette rather than the glow painting over foreground blocks. The earlier build drew the veil after the world and depth-tested a flat billboard at one world depth, which cut a hard line across the fogged terrain and framed the glow against the sky beyond the fog band; drawing it behind the world removes that frame and keeps the radial falloff of `ldx_sun_glare` continuous.

sections.title: Partial-Shape Blocks No Longer Bury Their Neighbors
items: `snapshot_for_chunk_build` in `src/ludoxel/simulation/worlds/state/world.py` now separates cell occupancy from face occlusion. A `full_occ` grid marks only cells filled by a full solid cube, resolved through the shared default block registry with `is_full_cube` and `is_solid`, and a cell counts as buried only when it is a full cube whose six neighbors are all full cubes. A slab, stair, fence, fence gate, or wall neighbor no longer covers a whole face, so a full block behind such a partial shape keeps its exposed face and is meshed, and a non-full-cube block always keeps its interior faces. The earlier grid treated every occupied cell as a full occluder, so a block sealed behind a partial shape was dropped from the chunk mesh and the view passed through it.

sections.title: Slabs Stack in Half-Block Steps
items: `place_from_hit_for_service` in `src/ludoxel/simulation/rules/interaction/placing.py` now chooses the added slab half from the exposed top or bottom face of the slab under the cursor, so a held slab completes the struck cell to a double rather than stepping a full cell and leaving a 0.5-block gap, even while the continuous-placement lock forces one half.

`_perform_vertical_slab_pillar` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/interface/viewport/controllers/interaction.py` drives the vertical build gesture for slabs: it fills a cell's second half before advancing to the next cell, so a held slab pillar rises in 0.5-block units without gaps. The earlier path applied the full-cube placement offset to slabs and stepped a whole cell for each one.

sections.title: Ultra Sun Disc, Veiling Glare, and Crepuscular Light
items: `ldx_ultra_sun` in `sun.frag` shapes the Ultra sun through coverage alone. The disc, core, and halo terms each decay to zero inside the billboard's inscribed circle, and an edge mask retires coverage before the quad border, so the square billboard no longer leaves a visible frame around the sun. The emitted color is a bright warm white that the falloffs do not pre-attenuate, so alpha blending over the sky brightens toward the disc and the dark ring the earlier weighting left around it is gone.

The Ultra tier dazzles the view when it faces the sun. `SunPass.draw_glare` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/opengl/passes/sun.py` and the matching draw in the WGPU backend place a camera-facing veil centered on the sun direction; `ldx_sun_glare` in `sun.frag` whitens the scene most strongly toward the sun and thins outward, and `sun_glare_strength` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/contracts/config.py` scales the veil by the squared view-to-sun alignment and the sun elevation, so it vanishes as the view turns away or the sun nears the horizon. The veil is depth-tested against the world depth buffer and writes no depth: the OpenGL pass enables the depth test and the WGPU path draws through `create_sun_glare_pipeline` with a `less` comparison, so geometry nearer than the sun occludes the glare and a block between the camera and the sun blocks the dazzle.

Distant terrain seen toward the sun gains warm in-scattered light. `ldx_apply_sun_shafts` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/shaders/common/distance_fog.glsl` weights that light by the geometry fog factor and the alignment of the view ray with the sun direction, so it rises only where a surface sits far enough to lie in the fog band and lines up with the sun; `world.frag` and `world_no_shadow.frag` apply it under the `u_ultra` gate.

The lower shadow-map quality tiers keep the simple sun billboard and the unmodified fog, while the Ultra tier draws the circular disc, the veiling glare, and the in-scattered light only when `shadow_quality` reaches `SHADOW_MAP_QUALITY_ULTRA`. The sun, glare, and world shaders are the shared GLSL that both the OpenGL and WGPU backends compile, and the WGPU dialect adaptation in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/wgpu/pipelines/factory.py` maps the new sun-mode and `u_ultra` uniforms so both backends carry the same effect.

sections.title: Ultra Cloud and Sun Rendering
items: `cloud_volume.frag` now evaluates Ultra cloud density as one occupied-cell union. It decodes the packed footprint, treats occupied neighbors as interior, and applies feathering only where the union meets empty space, so shared borders inside one `CloudField` cluster no longer become visible cell walls.

The Ultra volume shader expands the raymarch proxy around the packed footprint and lets feathered noise extend past the flat cell-face boundary. The material combines union-distance coverage, multi-scale noise erosion, soft vertical shaping, and warmer sunlight so L, T, notched, and stepped clusters read as one vapor mass instead of clipped boxes or a plain oval.
`sun.frag` keeps lower tiers on the existing simple billboard and uses the Ultra gate for a circular sun disc with a stronger warm halo.

sections.title: Othello Classic Search in the Native Engine
items: The weak, medium, and strong Othello difficulties search through the compiled Rust engine. `classic_root_scores` in `native/ludoxel_othello/src/engine.rs` mirrors the float evaluation terms, the position-weight move ordering, the pass rule, and the terminal values of `_alpha_beta` and the root loop of `_best_move` in `src/ludoxel/simulation/spaces/othello/engines/classic.py`. `_root_move_scores` selects the compiled module through `native_classic_root_scores` in `engines/native.py`, the pure Python loop stays the fallback owner, and the seeded tie selection remains in Python, so the chosen move is identical on both paths. The previous release routed only the insane difficulties through the native engine and searched the classic difficulties in pure Python.

Both Rust crates compile again under the locked PyO3 0.29. `native/ludoxel_othello/src/lib.rs` and `native/ludoxel_terrain/src/lib.rs` call `Python::detach`, the current name of the former `allow_threads`, so `npm run build:native` rebuilds both artifacts; the previous sources failed to compile against the locked dependency and left stale artifacts installed.

sections.title: Othello Candidate Evaluations in the Graph
items: `OthelloAnalysis` carries `move_evaluations`: one scored entry per legal root move, filled by every difficulty in `classic.py` and taken from `InsaneAnalysis.move_evaluations` on the insane paths. `_analysis_graph_samples` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/interface/othello/viewport.py` plots those candidates whenever an analysis holds fewer than two depth samples, so the weak and medium graphs show one real evaluation point per legal move; a position with a single legal move still shows a single point.

sections.title: Othello AI Off the UI Thread and Settled Saves
items: `OthelloAiWorker` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/interface/othello/worker.py` runs its in-process fallback on a dedicated worker thread: the move, analysis, and book-learning fallbacks submit to a `ThreadPoolExecutor` and return through the same pending-future poll as the process-pool path. The previous fallback executed the search synchronously on the UI thread, which froze the render loop, the thinking banner, and the disc flip animations while the AI computed.

Saving keeps a running flip animation intact. `settled_game_state` in `src/ludoxel/simulation/spaces/othello/matches/controller.py` resolves the pending animation and turn transition on a copy, and `save_state` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/interface/viewport/lifecycle/state.py` persists that copy while the live match state keeps animating.

sections.title: Cloud Cluster Footprints and Ultra Volumetric Clouds
items: Each cloud is a cluster of occupied cells on a per-cloud grid instead of a single rectangle. `CloudField` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/visuals/worlds/cloud_field.py` fills a solid core, notches corners, and attaches edge bumps, keeps the largest connected component, and produces L, T, notched, and stepped footprints that are always contiguous and at most four cells per axis.

The flat and wireframe tiers draw only the exterior cell faces. `cloud_face_rows` emits a face instance for a cell side only when the neighbouring cell is empty, and always for the top and bottom, so the six face buckets form one merged cloud surface with no interior faces: the wireframe shows the merged silhouette rather than overlapping box frames, and the solid cloud has no doubled internal walls. Both backends draw the same face buckets.

Ultra clouds are gated on the existing Shadow map quality setting: the OpenGL frame pipeline and the WGPU backend draw the volumetric path only when `shadow_quality` reaches `SHADOW_MAP_QUALITY_ULTRA`, and every lower tier keeps the flat cell-face path. No separate shader-quality preference is added.

The Ultra path renders each cloud as one translucent volume. `cloud_volume_rows` emits a single bounding box per cloud that carries the occupancy bitmask and grid dimensions; `cloud_volume.vert`/`cloud_volume.frag` march the view ray through that box and integrate an animated value-noise fbm density masked by the cell occupancy, so the volume uses the cluster footprint instead of a single oval and stays see-through. The noise domain scrolls with `u_time`, so the whole cloud keeps churning in place. The volumes are drawn back to front without depth writes so distant clouds remain visible through nearer ones.

A cloud size preference joins the Clouds settings. `normalize_cloud_cell_size` in `src/ludoxel/application/preferences/clouds.py` bounds the cell size to eight through forty blocks with a default of twenty; the value persists in the settings schema, projects into `BackendRendererRuntimeState`, and reaches `CloudField.set_cell_size` on both backends. The cloud density preference now changes the number of clouds: the macro cell that hosts one cloud shrinks and the drop threshold falls as density rises, so raising density from one to four multiplies the cloud count.

Cloud speed varies per cloud. `CloudField` quantizes the configured speed range into twelve multipliers and assigns each whole macro row perpendicular to the flow axis one multiplier, so rows own disjoint bands and clouds of different base speeds never drift into each other; a per-cloud turbulence sway in the vertex stage keeps clouds inside one row moving differently. Footprints stay inside their macro cell, so clouds of the same speed can never overlap.

The default cloud altitude is y = 128. `DEFAULT_CLOUD_FIXED_Y`, the spawn range 128 to 135, and the preferred interval 128 to 130 in `src/ludoxel/application/preferences/clouds.py` feed the settings defaults, the reset values, and the fallback for missing preference keys; a stored preference keeps its saved value. The default cloud `thickness` rises from 3 to 12 blocks, and each cloud varies between 0.85 and 1.3 times that value.

Clouds fade on their own horizontal range. `cloud_far_distance` and `cloud_fog_range` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/contracts/config.py` extend cloud visibility to at least 256 blocks and three times the render-distance radius, and both the OpenGL and the WGPU backend draw clouds with a dedicated far plane from `cloud_projection_z_far`, so the cloud fade is decoupled from the world render-distance fog and the world camera far plane.

sections.title: My World Loading Readiness
items: `visible_load_progress` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/uploads/world.py` gates world entry on the full render distance: the loading overlay stays up until every content chunk inside the render radius is built and resident. The previous gate admitted play after a three-chunk radius and left the remaining chunk builds and uploads running during the first seconds of play.

sections.title: Othello Infinite Flat Floor
items: The Othello play space stands on generation-backed flat terrain. `create_othello_session` builds its world through `make_othello_world_state` in `src/ludoxel/simulation/spaces/othello/game/board.py`, whose flat `WorldGenerationSpec` at ground level 0 resolves the grass floor procedurally at every coordinate; the checkerboard from `ensure_othello_board_layout` sits on that floor as placed blocks. The previous world was a materialized 97-by-97 static block grid from `generate_flat_world`, and beyond its edge the space was void; `generate_flat_world` is removed.

State restoration converts legacy Othello saves to the same contract. `_replace_othello_world` in `src/ludoxel/application/persistence/schedulers/state.py` detects a persisted static Othello world, reinstates the flat generation spec, and drops persisted floor cells whose state equals the flat base through `strip_othello_flat_floor_blocks`, so a save written before this release regains the unbounded floor while its board layer and edits survive.

sections.title: Normal World Chunk Loading and the Bedrock Envelope
items: `WorldState.visible_content_chunk_keys` selects render candidates from four bounded sets: the full vertical surface band of every column inside the horizontal render radius, the bedrock floor row of every such column, the three-by-three-by-three chunk neighborhood around the player, and every chunk with tracked mesh state — placed blocks, broken cells, or a mesh revision advanced by a neighboring edit — filtered horizontally. The previous selection clamped the surface band against the player's chunk Y and admitted only band or directly edited chunks, so crossing a sixteen-block chunk boundary, or breaking into a neighboring chunk, left terrain unloaded until that chunk itself was edited.

`chunk_has_content` reports the whole generated solid span between the content floor and the column band top: buried chunks mesh to zero faces until an edit exposes them, and the bedrock layer at y = -65 uploads its permanently exposed underside the same way the surface skin uploads its top. Flat generation collapses `_chunk_column_band` to the single ground layer, and `_mark_chunks_dirty` advances past the implicit first revision so the first edit of a pristine generated chunk always supersedes its resident mesh.

`within_render_distance` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/visuals/selections/chunk.py` bounds drawn chunks horizontally only. The vertical extent of drawable chunks is fixed by the upload tracker's resident set, so the surface stays visible from bedrock depth and the bedrock underside stays visible from below; the WGPU backend already drew every resident chunk, and the OpenGL predicate now matches that behavior.

sections.title: Rust Othello Search Engine
items: A new Rust crate at `native/ludoxel_othello` implements the Othello insane-search hot path — bitboard shifts, legal-move and flip resolution, the positional, corner, frontier, mobility, parity, and disc evaluation, move ordering, the negamax search, and the exact endgame solver — behind a PyO3 `cdylib` with internal transposition tables that follow the same soft-limit clearing policy as the Python cache. The compiled module imports as `ludoxel.simulation.spaces.othello.engines._othello_native`; ties round to even exactly as Python `round`, and primitives, evaluations, fixed-depth searches, and exact endgame solves return values bit-identical to the pure Python implementation, which remains the fallback owner in `search.py`.

`InsaneSearchCache` holds one native search session per cache through `ensure_native_search`; `_root_move_evaluations` routes each root move's subtree into the compiled `negamax` and `solve_exact` and reads the root ordering hint from the native transposition table. A deadline overrun raises the same `TimeoutError` the Python search raises, so iterative deepening in `analyze_insane_position` truncates identically; within the same time budget the compiled subtree search reaches greater depths. `npm run build:native` and `npm run build:native:check` cover the crate through the `RUST_NATIVE_MODULES` registry, the desktop build declares the module as a PyInstaller hidden import, wheel package data admits the installed artifact, and `MANIFEST.in` carries the crate source while pruning its `target` output.

The My World route planner in `src/ludoxel/simulation/actors/ai_players/planner.py` stays in Python: its transition validity is owned by the block-model contract — `has_full_top_support_for_block` and per-state collision boxes — and by the composed mutable world state, so a compiled port would either duplicate the whole block-shape rule set or call back into Python for every neighbor probe.

sections.title: Concurrent Sound Delivery
items: `PcmOneShotMixer` mixes attack one-shots through NumPy array operations instead of a per-sample Python loop, opens its `QAudioSink` with an explicit 4096-frame buffer, and refills every free frame of that buffer on each pump tick. The pump runs on the GUI thread, so the enlarged buffer and vectorized mix absorb render stalls that previously drained the sink mid-swing and broke the attack stream audibly while walking.

The pooled `QSoundEffect` path reclaims the oldest playing voice of the selected source when every voice is busy, through `steal_oldest_effect_slot` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/audio/playback/effects.py`. An admitted event — a footstep landing between swings, a block action during rapid placement — now always reaches a voice; previously `_play_effect_pool` dropped the event and the mix lost sounds under load.

sections.title: Respawn Follows the Loaded World
items: Loading a My World now resynchronizes `SessionSettings.spawn_x`, `spawn_y`, `spawn_z`, and `seed` from the loaded world's generation spec through `spawn_for_generation`, in `load_my_world_space_into_session` and in the startup state restore. `SessionManager.respawn` therefore places the player on the loaded world's own spawn column. Previously the spawn settings kept the startup session's normal-terrain spawn, which for a flat world sat below the ground layer, so every death respawned the player into the void and the fall repeated without end.

sections.title: World Library Grid Width
items: `WorldGridCard` fixes its width to the thumbnail width plus the card margins and renders the world name through an eliding label that never requests width for its text, so a long world name truncates with an ellipsis — the full name stays available as a tooltip — instead of widening the card. `MyWorldLibraryPage` derives its column arithmetic from the exported card width, and `WorldListRow` elides its name the same way.

sections.title: Rust Terrain Binding Dependency Update
items: The `ludoxel_terrain` crate now builds against PyO3 0.25.1 instead of 0.23.5. The upgrade moves the binding past the three published PyO3 advisories affecting versions before 0.24.1: the out-of-bounds read in the `nth` and `nth_back` implementations of the `PyList` and `PyTuple` iterators, the missing `Sync` bound on `PyCFunction::new_closure` closures, and the buffer-overflow risk in `PyString::from_object`. The terrain binding itself calls none of those APIs — it exposes three `#[pyfunction]` entry points returning bytes — so the change removes the vulnerable dependency versions from the build without altering the module contract.

`native/ludoxel_terrain/Cargo.toml` records the crate version as `3.7.7-Hotfix.1`, and `native_build_info()` reports that string through the compiled module. The binding API, the `abi3-py311` stable-ABI configuration, the artifact placement, and the `build:native` and `build:native:check` behavior are unchanged.

sections.title: Terrain Noise Channel Naming
items: The per-purpose discriminator that separates the terrain noise fields — height octaves, ravine fields, strata selection, and ore gates — is now named `channel` instead of `salt` in `native/ludoxel_terrain/src/terrain.rs` and `src/ludoxel/simulation/worlds/generation/terrain_math.py`. The value is a procedural noise-lane selector mixed into the deterministic world hash, not cryptographic material, and the previous name caused static analysis to classify the incrementing channel constant as a hard-coded cryptographic salt.

The rename is lexical only: the hash function, the channel constants, the evaluation order, and every generated value are unchanged, the Rust and Python implementations remain bit-identical for identical inputs, and existing seeded worlds reproduce the same terrain.

sections.title: Seeded My World Creation
items: Create New World now selects a world type and a seed in addition to the world name and game mode. `WorldCreatePage` adds a Normal/Flat toggle and a seed field pre-filled with `1`; an empty field resolves to seed `1`, an explicit `0` is stored and restored as `0`, and a non-integer or out-of-64-bit-range entry disables Create. The confirmed name, game mode, generation mode, and seed travel through `StartupShellOverlay` and the viewport menu controller into `WorldGenerationSpec` and `WorldLibraryStore.create_world`.

Normal mode generates deterministic terrain from the seed, the generation version, and the world coordinate: four bounded value-noise octaves keep adjacent surface columns within one block of each other, a masked ridge field carves meandering ravines whose surfaces expose stone, a bedrock layer sits at y = -65, and dirt, coarse dirt, gravel, stone variants, deepslate, and registered ore blocks are mixed through noise fields rather than axis-aligned clusters. `validate_terrain_materials` raises at session construction when a terrain material id is not registered.

Flat mode is an explicit Create New World selection rather than an implicit default; the previous fixed 65-by-65 flat map path through `generate_test_map` is removed, and `make_my_world_state` now builds a world from a generation spec. The Othello play space keeps its own fixed flat board world through `create_othello_session`.

The initial player position for a normal-mode world comes from `spawn_for_generation` in the simulation layer, which scans outward from the origin for a ravine-free column whose neighbors differ by at most one block; flat mode spawns above its ground level and legacy static worlds keep the previous fixed spawn.

sections.title: World State Edit Delta and Persistence
items: `WorldState` is now a current-state resolver over three layers: user-placed blocks answer first, recorded broken base-terrain coordinates answer as air, and the deterministic base terrain answers last. Breaking a base-terrain block records its coordinate; breaking a placed block removes only the placed record and keeps an underlying broken record, so broken terrain does not resurface after building and removing a block in the same cell, and a block placed into open air leaves no broken record when removed.

The `world.blocks` view keeps `get`, containment, and indexing over the composed state, so picking, placing, breaking, collision, gravity, selection, and the third-person camera resolve unmaterialized base terrain without enumerating it; finite enumeration through `keys` and `items` is limited to placed blocks. The AI route planner no longer receives a full world snapshot: `AiPlayerManager` builds a bounded planning window around the actor and its route points through `snapshot_block_window`, and gravity column scans read a bounded composite column instead of a finite block dictionary.

`.ldxworld` packages now carry a version-2 world payload holding the generation spec, the revision, `placed` rows, and `broken` rows; `LDXWORLD_FORMAT_VERSION` and `WORLD_ENTRY_FILE_VERSION` move to 2. A version-1 payload with a materialized `blocks` list still loads, as a static generation spec whose blocks become placed rows, and the next save normalizes it to the current schema. No migration path reads the retired `state/world_state.json` or `state/player_state.json` files.

sections.title: Surface Envelope Rendering Uploads
items: `WorldUploadTracker` selects chunks from `WorldState.visible_content_chunk_keys` instead of the existing-block chunk index. Per-chunk-column content bands derived from bulk surface heights bound which chunks exist to render, `snapshot_for_chunk_build` materializes one 18-cubed box per chunk and emits only exposed cells as face sources with a one-cell state margin for occlusion, and materialization runs inside the mesh-build worker thread rather than on the render thread.

The loading gate counts content chunks within the initial gate radius and closes only when each is resident in the renderer backend at its current mesh revision; a zero denominator closes the loader only when the world genuinely reports no content chunks in range. The loading status line shows ready/total chunks with the pending build count and, after four seconds without progress, appends the tracker stall detail naming pending and resident counts and the last scheduled, built, and uploaded chunk.

sections.title: Rust Native Terrain Engine
items: A new Rust crate at `native/ludoxel_terrain` implements the terrain hot path — deterministic hashing, 2D and 3D value noise, surface heights, ravine carving, and material selection — behind a PyO3 `cdylib` built with the stable ABI. The compiled module imports as `ludoxel.simulation.worlds.generation._terrain_native` and returns C-order `int32` height bytes and `uint8` material bytes; `native.py` owns the guarded import and `fallback.py` carries the identical pure-Python contract, verified bit-equal across seeds, modes, and coordinates.

`tools/build_native_extensions` now dispatches two native families: the existing Cython candidates and the Rust crate target. `npm run build:native` runs `cargo build --release` and installs the cdylib as `_terrain_native.pyd` (or `.so`), and `npm run build:native:check` imports the compiled module with `PYTHONPATH` pinned to the repository source tree, requiring `__file__` to resolve under `src/ludoxel` with the platform's compiled suffix; the Python fallback never passes that check, and stale crate sources are reported with a rebuild instruction.

The desktop build declares the terrain module as a PyInstaller hidden import for both platforms, wheel package data admits the installed artifact, and `MANIFEST.in` carries the crate source while pruning its `target` output. Application startup performs only the guarded import; it never runs cargo, a rebuild, or a bulk self-test.

sections.title: My World Menu Spacing
items: My World library, Edit World, and PAUSE overlay buttons now share the `interface/common` menu-button helper for controls that use `#menuBtn`, and the grid/list card edit buttons use the same widget-rectangle layout attribute. The buttons lay out against their widget rectangles, so native push-button insets do not collapse the visual gaps around the Grid/List toggle, Import World, Create New World, Export (.ldxworld), Delete World, Cancel, and destructive confirmation buttons. The visual button styling remains in QSS.

The Delete World confirmation panel now reserves lower space through its `QVBoxLayout` margins and gives the label-to-button row a structural gap, so the Cancel/Delete row no longer sits flush against the panel bottom.

sections.title: World Thumbnail Cache and Packages
items: The active My World thumbnail cache is refreshed at explicit exit boundaries rather than from the save path. Before the PAUSE overlay is shown, and before direct viewport shutdown, the viewport crops the still-visible My World widget with `QScreen.grabWindow`, encodes that image with `encode_thumbnail_png`, and keeps only cached bytes for `save_state`. If no cache exists, the world body still saves and `WorldLibraryStore.save_space` preserves the thumbnail already in the package.
`encode_thumbnail_png` now keeps the `QByteArray` backing its `QBuffer` alive while `QImage.save` writes the PNG bytes, so thumbnail encoding does not depend on a temporary Qt buffer object.

The world thumbnail path does not add an OpenGL framebuffer readback, does not require WGPU surface copy-source usage, and does not change the renderer `render` contract. Switching My Worlds passes the outgoing world's cached thumbnail to `save_space` and clears the cache for the selected world, preventing a previous world's image from being saved onto the next entry.

The `.ldxworld` thumbnail member now remains connected across the visible library path: summaries read `thumbnail.png`, grid cards and list rows display those bytes inside their fixed thumbnail slots, export writes the stored thumbnail, and import passes the package thumbnail into the newly created library entry.

sections.title: Windows Package Build
items: The Windows PyInstaller command now writes a generated `hook-OpenGL.py` beside the generated spec. The hook keeps PyOpenGL platform and array discovery while leaving OpenGL DLL data collection empty, and the spec guard drops cached `OpenGL/DLLS`, `MSVCR90.dll`, or `MSVCR100.dll` entries if they appear.

sections.title: Shared Renderer Shader Source
items: The OpenGL and WGPU backends now read one shader source instead of two copies. The stage files and the `common/` includes that were duplicated under `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/opengl/shaders/` and `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/wgpu/shaders/sources/` are consolidated into `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/shaders/`, and `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/shaders/source.py` owns the root resolution and `#include` expansion through `shader_source_root`, `expand_shader_source`, and `load_shader_source`. The two separate include-expansion helpers in the backends are removed.

`GLResources.load` and `ShaderProgram.from_files` compile the shared GLSL 330 directly, while `factory._wgpu_glsl_source` loads the same files through `load_shader_source` and applies `_adapt_wgpu_glsl` to add the explicit varying locations, the `set = 0` uniform blocks, the split texture and sampler bind-group entries, and the `#version 450` rewrite that wgpu-native requires. The fog uniform declarations and the `v_worldPos` varying location that the deleted WGPU copies carried pre-edited are now produced by the adaptation, so the adapted WGPU modules and the compiled OpenGL programs reproduce their previous text from the single source.

The shader contract checker, package data, and macOS bundle inputs follow the move. `tools/check_project/src/check/shaders/shaders.check.mjs` scans the single `presentation/rendering/shaders` root, the `pyproject.toml` package-data globs and `MANIFEST.in` list one shader path, and `macos-status.service.mjs` requires the shared `world.vert` and `world.frag`.

sections.title: WGPU Color Target Contrast
items: The macOS WGPU surface no longer stores fragment output through an sRGB encode that the OpenGL backend does not apply. `configure_wgpu_canvas` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/backends/wgpu/runtime/surface.py` passed the adapter-preferred format straight to `context.configure`; on the Metal path that format carries a `-srgb` suffix, so the surface applied a linear-to-sRGB encode on write. The world, cloud, sun, Othello, and first-person shaders compute lighting and fog on the raw `rgba8unorm` atlas, matching the OpenGL `GL_RGBA` atlas, so the extra encode lifted midtones and lowered contrast relative to the OpenGL output.

`linear_color_target_format` now drops a trailing `-srgb` suffix from the preferred format, and the configured surface and every pipeline color target use that non-sRGB format. Fragment output is stored without the encode, matching the OpenGL default framebuffer, so the shared lighting, fog, shadow, and selection math is stored with the same encoding on both backends.

sections.title: My World Switch Render State
items: Entering a different My World now reconstructs the visible chunks from the current world's own blocks before any block is placed or broken. `WorldUploadTracker` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/rendering/uploads/world.py` keyed its chunk-mesh build cache by `id(world)`, and the My World session reuses one `WorldState` object across world loads, so the meshes built for a previous My World could satisfy the first upload of the next one and the entered world showed the prior world's blocks until a later edit forced a fresh mesh.

`WorldState` in `src/ludoxel/simulation/worlds/state/world.py` now carries a process-monotonic `content_generation` that advances on construction and on every `replace_all`. A full content swap restarts `revision` and the per-chunk mesh revisions from a small value, so this generation is the world identity the upload tracker uses as its cache key, and meshes from one loaded world no longer alias another loaded into the same object.

`WorldUploadTracker.reset`, which runs on every play-space switch and My World load, now also drops its cached chunk meshes so a superseded generation cannot be replayed into the incoming world. The OpenGL and WGPU backends already evict every GPU-side chunk on that reset, so the single upload-tracker correction covers both renderer paths, and a coordinate that held a block in the previous My World no longer renders as transparent residue in the entered one.

sections.title: macOS Pause Button Spacing
items: The pause overlay buttons now lay out against their own widget rectangle. The macOS native style insets push-button layout-item rectangles to reserve room for the Aqua focus ring, and that inset was subtracted from the pause panel's `QVBoxLayout` spacing, collapsing the gaps between Resume, Settings, Play My World, Play Othello (Reversi), and Save & Quit to zero on macOS while Windows kept its spacing. `PauseOverlay` in `src/ludoxel/presentation/interface/overlays/pause.py` sets `WA_LayoutUsesWidgetRect` on its `#menuBtn` buttons through one shared constructor, so the structural button and skin-action spacing holds identically on macOS and Windows.

The change keeps the single pause overlay and leaves the button order, labels, and the Play My World, Play Othello (Reversi), and Save & Quit save-then-navigate behavior intact. Button color, border, radius, hover, and pressed styling remain in the `#menuBtn` QSS.

sections.title: Startup Menu Balance
items: The startup menu now computes the Play My World, Play Othello (Reversi), and Quit button panel from the page width alone, keeping the central menu button box centered at the minimum 1040 by 700 desktop window size.

The changelog notification button is positioned in the lower-left side region between the app edge and the centered menu panel, while the player profile panel is positioned in the lower-right side region between the menu panel and the app edge. The profile panel no longer touches the central button box.

The creator label and runtime version label are fixed to the bottom edge instead of being lifted by a vertical root layout. The profile panel is bottom-anchored above the version label and keeps the fixed 300 by 360 pixel skin preview visible together with the Change Skin and Reset to Alex buttons.

MenuProfilePanel uses compact fixed-size action spacing, and PlayerSkinPreviewWidget keeps a fixed preview size. Short menu heights no longer alter the rendered skin size or hide the upper preview area and lower skin action buttons.

sections.title: Shared Play-Space Exit and Save
items: Leaving the active play-space now runs through one boundary. `_exit_active_play_space` saves the current My World and Othello through `viewport.save_state` and only advances on success, and Save & Quit, the pause Play My World button, and the pause Play Othello (Reversi) button all use it. The pause Play My World and Play Othello paths previously switched without saving, so block placement, player position, inventory, health, AI actors, and world settings for My World, and board, match, and turn state for Othello, are now written before the play-space is left.

The save no longer reports success when the active world cannot be written. `AppStateStore.save` raises when `WorldLibraryStore.save_space` fails, the world-data save is allowed to propagate out of `viewport.save_state`, and the exit boundary catches a failure, shows a notification, logs the traceback, and stays in the current play-space instead of advancing. The previous `try/except Exception: pass` that hid Save & Quit failures is removed.

Returning to the startup menu after a save is deferred to the next event-loop pass and guarded, so the pause button that triggered it is not torn down inside its own handler and a navigation error is logged rather than aborting the process.

Auxiliary save steps are isolated from the world write. A failure in the renderer sun read, the Othello animation settle, or the framebuffer thumbnail grab is logged and skipped, and a thumbnail capture failure no longer counts as a world-data save failure.

sections.title: World Package Write Path
items: Saving the active world reads only the package manifest and thumbnail rather than decompressing the full world body. `WorldLibraryStore.save_space` resolves the preserved name, created time, and thumbnail from `read_world_package_summary` and writes the new `PersistedPlaySpace`, narrowing the window in which the `state/worlds/<id>.ldxworld` file is held open.

`export_world_package` retries the final `os.replace` when it fails transiently and raises `LdxworldError` if it cannot finalize, and a failed write removes its temporary file rather than leaving a partial package. An unreadable package is reported as absent by the library reads, so a single corrupt world cannot crash a library rebuild.

sections.title: Startup Menu Profile Preview
items: The skin preview now reacts to the pointer across the whole startup menu page. `StartupMenuPage` installs the pointer event filter and forwards press, move, release, and leave events to the shared `PlayerSkinPreviewWidget`, using the page extent for head and body tracking. The forwarding leaves clicks intact, so Play My World, Play Othello (Reversi), Quit, Change Skin, Reset to Alex, and the changelog button still receive their own input while the model turns toward the cursor.

The menu skin preview no longer slides into the Change Skin and Reset to Alex buttons at short window heights. `PlayerSkinPreviewWidget` carries a Preferred size policy with a lower minimum box, and the profile panel lets the preview yield height before the buttons, so the box shrinks and keeps the full model rendered inside it at the minimum window height. The model is fit to a fixed vertical field of view, so a shorter box shows the whole model smaller rather than clipping the legs.

sections.title: My World Grid Layout
items: The world grid wraps from its first appearance. `MyWorldLibraryPage` defers the column computation to the first show and recomputes it once the scroll viewport reports a width, replacing the single-column layout that formed while the viewport width was still zero.

Resizing the grid reflows the existing cards. A resize is debounced through a single-shot timer, recomputes the column count, and repositions the same `WorldGridCard` widgets only when the count changes. Cards are no longer reparented to `None` and recreated, removing the momentary top-level windows that appeared while the grid rebuilt on every resize.

The grid column count subtracts the content margins and the vertical scroll bar width before dividing by the card-plus-spacing width, so the right card column stays inside the scroll viewport at small widths, at full width, and while the vertical scroll bar is shown.
Grid and List are an exclusive checked pair. The two view toggles share a `QButtonGroup`, and the active view's toggle holds the checked state that the theme stylesheet paints.

sections.title: In-Application World Creation and Editing
items: Create New World and Edit World are screens inside the startup shell. `WorldCreatePage` holds the name field, the Survival and Creative toggle, and Create, and returns to the library with the created world present. `WorldEditPage` retitles itself `Edit <name>` and carries the rename field, Export (.ldxworld), and a delete confirmation rendered inside the screen. Each screen returns to the My World library through the shared `ScreenTitleBar` back control.
The `WorldCreateDialog` and `WorldRenameDialog` classes, the per-world `QMenu` of rename, export, and delete actions, and the `QMessageBox` delete confirmation are removed.

Creating, renaming, and importing a world no longer refuse a name that matches another world. Worlds are identified by `world_id`, so duplicate display names are accepted on every path; only an empty or whitespace-only name is refused at creation and rename. `WorldLibraryStore.existing_names` is removed.

Delete removes the selected world and is no longer forced to keep one world. `delete_world` deletes the package and clears the active-world pointer, and deleting the last world leaves an empty library; the store recreates a default world only on a first launch where no library index exists yet, so loading or saving an intentionally empty library no longer repopulates it.

sections.title: Pause and Menu Navigation
items: Pause Play My World opens the My World library page. It closes the pause overlay and shows the startup shell on the library page rather than starting the active world, so a specific world is entered only by selecting it in the library.
Pause Save & Quit saves and returns to the startup menu. It writes the current state through `save_state` and opens the startup menu through `open_startup_menu` instead of closing the window.

The startup menu adds a Quit button. `StartupMenuPage` emits a quit request that closes the main window, and the window close path runs the existing shutdown and final save. Application exit is no longer reached from the pause Save & Quit button.

sections.title: Chat Title Bar
items: The Chat and Commands screen uses the shared `ScreenTitleBar`, so its `< Back` control matches the My World screen back button. The chat-specific title bar frame, title label, and back-button styles are removed while the chat input, settings button, send button, candidate view, and history scroll keep their bottom-bar layout.

sections.title: Per-World and Othello Player State
items: Each My World is stored as its own `state/worlds/<id>.ldxworld` package and is updated on every save. `WorldLibraryStore` reads and writes the same archive format used for export and import, so the package holds that world's player, world blocks, AI actors, the `PersistedWorldInventory` hotbar with its 9x3 upper storage and AI route hotbar, and the world thumbnail. The previous shared inventory is gone; switching worlds captures the leaving world into its package and restores the selected world's inventory into the runtime through `apply_world_inventory_to_runtime`.

The save path writes one world package per save. The active world's thumbnail is captured once and passed through `save_state` and `AppStateStore.save` into `WorldLibraryStore.save_space`, which preserves the existing thumbnail when none is supplied, so saving no longer rewrites the world twice. The renderer sun read, the Othello animation settle, and the framebuffer thumbnail grab are isolated from the persistence call, so a failure in any auxiliary step can no longer prevent the world and settings from being written.

Othello carries no saved inventory. `PersistedOthelloSpace` holds the board, player, AI actors, and `OthelloGameState`; the Othello runtime hotbar is rebuilt from its defaults each launch and is not written to disk.

The global runtime file is `state/app_state.json`. `AppStateStore` writes the last active space, the display and control settings, the standing Othello settings, and the Othello play space there, while each world package owns its own player, world, inventory, and AI actors. The `state/player_state.json` and `state/world_state.json` files and their readers are removed, and the runtime integrity manifest protects `state/app_state.json` in place of the two old files.

sections.title: Startup Menu Admission
items: Loading no longer enters the previously saved play-space. The first time the viewport finishes loading, `_finish_loading` opens a startup menu, and `ViewportOverlays.set_menu_open` holds the gameplay HUD, mouse capture, and fixed-step input behind a menu modal. A saved active space is restored only after its play button is pressed, so a save whose last active space was My World or Othello still lands on the menu.

The startup menu carries the Ludoxel logo, a creator label, the runtime version label, a notification button on the lower left, and a player profile panel on the lower right. The profile panel reuses the pause skin preview with the same Change Skin and Reset to Alex actions and writes through the same saved skin state. The button panel offers Play My World and Play Othello (Reversi).

sections.title: My World Library
items: Play My World opens a My World library rather than starting a single world. `MyWorldLibraryPage` lists each world with a thumbnail, the current Survival or Creative game mode, the created and updated dates, and the on-disk world size, and toggles between a grid and a list view. Create New World adds a world after a name and a game mode are chosen and returns to the library with the world present rather than entering gameplay; a per-world action menu provides rename, delete, and export, with rename rejecting empty, whitespace, and duplicate names and delete requiring confirmation.

Each My World is stored as its own runtime file. `WorldLibraryStore` owns `state/world_library.json`, the per-world `state/worlds/<id>.json` entries, the per-world game mode, and the active-world pointer, and the My World save path writes the active world's player, world blocks, and AI actors into its own entry. Othello state remains separate and is never placed in the My World library.

sections.title: World Thumbnails
items: Saving a My World captures the rendered frame as that world's thumbnail. `_capture_active_world_thumbnail` reads the viewport framebuffer on the save path, encodes a PNG into the world's runtime data through `WorldLibraryStore.write_thumbnail_bytes`, and the library shows it as the world's image. Thumbnails are user runtime data tracked by the runtime integrity manifest, not bundled assets.

sections.title: Ludoxel World Packages
items: Worlds export and import as `.ldxworld` packages. `export_world_package` writes a validated zip holding the package manifest, the persisted world state, and the thumbnail, and `read_world_package` validates the format and rejects a malformed package without changing the existing library. A `.ldxworld` path passed on the command line or forwarded to a running instance through single-instance activation is validated and imported into the library.

sections.title: In-Application Changelog
items: The notification button opens the changelog inside the application. The changelog viewer reads a packaged changelog resource and renders the same dated entries published on the website. The desktop resource is generated from the website changelog data and a sync check compares the two, so the in-application changelog and the website changelog cannot diverge silently.

sections.title: AI Settings Learning Loader
items: Selecting the Learning tab now shows the same loader structure used by the Settings About tab before the learning controls are built. Controller creation, policy option enumeration, dataset summary reading, and policy path resolution run on a worker thread, then the Learning page is assembled on the UI thread from the loaded snapshot.

sections.title: Chat Suggestions and Mentions
items: Command and mention suggestions now hide the chat message list while the candidate view is open and keep the candidate view aligned to the lower edge of the chat display area. Mention suggestions consume Enter to confirm the selected `@Name` before any message submission can run, while slash-command suggestions keep Enter available for submitting the current command text.

Typing an `@` token now opens the same suggestion view with the local player and live AI names. Selecting a candidate replaces the current token with `@Name`, and the local chat display derives yellow text for exact local-player `@Name` mentions without writing formatting controls into the raw message text.

sections.title: AI Route Overlay
items: Completed AI route overlays now derive a deterministic presentation color from the route owner actor id. The completed path segments, closed-loop segment, point markers, and matching AI name text use the same owner color while the route-edit draft remains the green dashed path.

Completed AI route overlays are now gated by the F3 Debug HUD visibility contract. Draft route-edit feedback remains visible during editing, while completed route paths and the matching AI name color are omitted when the Debug HUD is hidden.

sections.title: AI Settings Open Path
items: Opening AI Settings after confirming a route, or by right-clicking an AI actor in Creative Mode, no longer constructs the AI learning controller, scans policy options, reads learning summaries, or decodes imported skin files before the Identity page is shown.

sections.title: Conservative Visibility Bounds
items: Cloud visibility now tests the shifted cloud box extents against the camera frustum. OpenGL and WGPU consume the same `CloudField.visible_boxes` result, and the shared culler skips a box only when the full rendered volume lies outside the view.

AI route overlays now clip each route segment against the view volume before drawing it. A segment stays visible while any part of it crosses the screen, even when an endpoint is outside the viewport.

sections.title: Support Callout and Input Resume
items: Changed the periodic support callout from `Project support: 5uog` to `Support the creator: 5uog`, keeping only the `5uog` span linked to `https://github.com/5uog/` through the existing chat link activation path.
Changed the support callout cadence from 120 seconds to 600 seconds.

Closing inventory, pause, chat, settings, AI settings, or a transient dialog now clears accumulated mouse delta and restores camera capture from the post-close cursor baseline. The first movement after capture resumes is admitted as the new gameplay delta source.

sections.title: Inventory Ambient Playback Continuity
items: Opening the inventory no longer disables the My World ambient source. `_ambient_audio_active` now treats the inventory as an input-neutral storage surface rather than an ambient reset boundary, so the existing ambient key, source rotation, and looping effect stay owned by the active `AudioManager` while storage is open.

Pause, death, loading, and the Othello settings surface remain ambient stop boundaries. Chat, inventory, the ordinary settings surface, AI settings, and hidden-HUD states leave the ambient loop controlled by the current play-space key and the saved ambient-volume preferences.

sections.title: Pooled Sound Playback Gain
items: Reused pooled `QSoundEffect` voices now receive the playback request gain immediately before `play()`. Slot preparation keeps only fixed effect setup, so a reused voice cannot retain a previous remote distance gain or a previous full-volume local request.

Remote world sound events keep the shared listener cutoff and distance gain route. AI block actions, AI damage-hit positions, player hits on AI targets, and gravity-broken block sounds now enter the remote playback entrance with a required world position and cached listener pose before a pooled slot is used.

Player local feedback remains outside distance attenuation. Player block placement, breaking, interaction, footsteps, landing, local damage, and Othello feedback use the local playback entrance, so a target or board position does not make immediate player feedback quieter or silent.

Material one-shot playback remains on immediate prepared `QSoundEffect` slots. The existing PCM mixer remains scoped to weak and strong attack feedback, and block, material, footstep, landing, damage, and Othello one-shots are not moved onto the `QAudioSink` stream path.

sections.title: AI Action Sounds
items: AI block placement, breaking, and fence-gate interaction now emit the same material sound events as the player. `AiPlayerManager` records each successful `InteractionOutcome` from its placement, break, and interact paths as an `AiBlockSoundEvent` holding the action, block state, and cell, returns them on `AiStepReport.block_sound_events`, and the render loop replays them through `AudioManager.play_ai_interaction` after the session step.

AI action sounds attenuate with listener distance. `play_ai_interaction` reuses the player block sound pools with attenuation enabled, and `_play_pool` scales the resolved volume by `spatial_distance_gain`, a linear rolloff from the listener to the pool `distance_cutoff`. The sound is loudest at the source, falls off with distance, and is dropped once the listener is past the audible radius.

sections.title: AI Placement Line of Sight
items: AI block placement requires the actor to face the target column with a clear line to it. `_placement_ray_clear` adds a horizontal facing test against `actor.player.view_forward()` bounded by `_AI_PLACEMENT_FACING_MIN_DOT` (cosine of 55 degrees) ahead of the existing occlusion ray, so a planner candidate is refused at the final mutation when the actor has turned away from the face or a block stands between the actor and the anchor.

sections.title: Strafe Model Pose
items: Player and AI models keep the forward and backward foot animation while strafing and turn the rendered body toward a pure left or right movement input without rotating the head. `PlayerMotionState.strafe_turn_deg` eases toward a bounded 18-degree yaw only when the current movement input has a lateral component and no forward or backward component; `build_player_model_snapshot` adds that offset to `body_yaw_deg` and counter-resolves `head_yaw_deg` so the visible head keeps its world-facing direction while the body, arms, legs, held item, and shadow rows follow the body turn.

sections.title: Rapid Placement Sound Selection
items: Rapid block placement plays the placed block material instead of dropping to the stone sound. `AudioManager.play_block_action` commits to the first sound group in `iter_sound_group_candidates` that defines a pool for the action and stops there, so an exhausted voice budget on the placed material no longer advances the candidate chain to the default stone pool.

sections.title: Player Health Regeneration
items: The Settings Player tab adds a Health Regeneration card with Regeneration, Start delay, Health cap, and Time to cap controls. `PlayerRegenParams` on `SessionSettings` owns the values, `PersistedSettings` persists them, and saves without the fields load disabled so existing worlds keep their current behavior.

After the player avoids damage for the start delay, `advance_player_regeneration` heals at `cap_hp / time_to_cap_s` per second up to the lesser of the cap and `max_health`. Damage resets the delay timer, and a disabled toggle leaves health unchanged.

sections.title: Inventory Preview Clearance
items: Increased the visible gap below the player preview by adding one storage gutter to the existing top-area clearance. `_TOP_AREA_TO_UPPER_GAP` now derives from `_TOP_AREA_CLEARANCE + _SLOT_GAP`, so `_TOP_AREA_HEIGHT` shortens the preview and crafting row while the 9x4 storage coordinates remain fixed.

sections.title: Inventory Layout Alignment
items: `_build_top_area` centers a storage-width row above the 9x4 storage, so the black-background player preview shares the storage left edge, spans the first three storage columns and the two gaps between them, and opens one panel margin below the box top, the same gap the hotbar row leaves above the box bottom.

The 2x2 crafting input, the arrow, and the read-only output sit centered between the preview box right edge and the storage right edge, and the 30x30 `closeBtn` moved to the top-right of that row with its right edge on the storage right edge. The crafting cluster is the only element that drops below the close button, so the preview and the 9x4 storage keep their positions.
Removed the full-width close-button header. The inventory preview widget now fills its black box at the box width and height, and the third-person model stays centered in it at that larger size.

sections.title: All Items Catalog and Survival Startup
items: Set the Creative All Items box to seven columns with a vertical-only scroll. Its fixed width holds the seven catalog columns beside the vertical scrollbar, and `_apply_filter` lays the entries out across seven columns with no horizontal scroll.

Stopped a stray AI Spawning Egg slot from drawing at the window top-left when Survival opened the inventory. Catalog buttons are now parented to the All Items scroll host, and `_apply_filter` hides every catalog button before placing the matches, so the Survival inventory and the filtered-out entries leave no button at the overlay origin.

sections.title: Inventory Preview Pointer Tracking
items: The inventory preview follows the pointer. The overlay event filter forwards mouse motion to `move_pointer`, and the inventory preview widget enables hover body tracking, so the model turns its head toward the cursor and adjusts its body yaw by a smaller amount; the composed preview state reads those angles through `preview_angles()`.

sections.title: macOS WGPU Inventory Preview Held Block
items: Added the third-person held block to the WGPU offscreen preview pass. `render_player_preview_frame` now draws `_third_person_held_block_face_rows(pose.held_block_pose)` with the atlas bind group after the skin, so the block in the selected hotbar slot appears and updates in the macOS inventory preview as it already did on the OpenGL preview path.

sections.title: Shared My World Storage
items: Unified the My World hotbar and 9x3 upper inventory into one shared thirty-six-slot storage state. Creative Mode now exposes the All Items catalog while Survival Mode hides it; switching modes retains the same central inventory, selected hotbar index, and HUD projection.

Replaced the duplicated Creative and Survival persistence branches with `my_world_hotbar_slots`, `my_world_selected_hotbar_index`, and `my_world_upper_slots`. The player-state reader normalizes a Beta 1 save once from the branch selected by its stored game mode, then subsequent saves emit only the shared My World fields while Othello and route-edit hotbars remain separate.

sections.title: Inventory Operations and Preview
items: Reserved a dedicated 30x30 close-button header in the central inventory box. The `close.svg` button remains fixed at the box top-right while the player preview and the 2x2 crafting input, arrow, and read-only output occupy the row below it.

Number keys now distinguish an infinite All Items catalog source from finite central storage. Catalog entries replace the target hotbar slot; hotbar, upper-inventory, and crafting-input sources move or swap atomically with the target, so the source no longer remains as a duplicate. The read-only crafting output is excluded from number-key assignment.

Inventory preview cache keys now include the skin and the held block or special-item fields consumed by the preview pose. Storage commits synchronize the first-person target, invalidate the inventory preview cache, and queue a repaint so held items disappear or appear in the preview as their selected hotbar slot changes.

Closing the inventory moves each crafting input item to the hotbar and then the upper inventory when space exists. A full central storage leaves the unplaced input item in the transient crafting grid instead of clearing it.

sections.title: 9x4 My World Inventory Storage
items: Expanded the My World inventory from a nine-slot hotbar to thirty-six storage slots per game mode: the nine-slot hotbar plus a 9x3 upper inventory of twenty-seven slots that stays hidden until the inventory opens. `RuntimePreferences` now carries `creative_upper_slots` and `survival_upper_slots` next to the existing per-mode hotbars, and the upper inventory orders its slots row-major from the top-left while the hotbar keeps indices 0 through 8 left to right.

Each storage slot still holds a single item id; the change adds slots rather than stack counts. `PersistedInventory` now serializes `creative_upper_slots` and `survival_upper_slots`, `runtime_state` carries those fields in both directions, and `PlayerStateFile` advanced to version 8.

Added a 2x2 crafting input and a 1x1 crafting output to the central box, kept apart from the thirty-six storage slots. The crafting input is a transient working area: closing the inventory moves each crafting item into the storage by hotbar-then-upper priority and leaves the grid empty, so the crafting grid is never persisted. The 1x1 output is read-only and resolves to empty because Ludoxel implements no crafting recipe resolution.

sections.title: Survival and Creative Inventory Layout
items: Rebuilt `InventoryOverlay` around a square central box that stacks the 9x3 upper inventory above the 9x1 hotbar row, places a black-background player preview on the upper left and the 2x2 crafting input and 1x1 output on the upper right, and carries a close button driven by `assets/ui/inventory/close.svg` in the top-right corner. Creative Mode adds an All Items box to the left of the central box that supplies every block and special item.
Search in the All Items box keeps filtered results in the same top-left row-major order as the full catalog, filling each row left to right before wrapping to the next.
Replaced the inventory title, subtitle, Survival-Mode notice, and the text close control with the slot layout and the `close.svg` icon button.

sections.title: Cursor Carry, Shift Transfer, and Slot Keys
items: A left click now lifts an item onto the cursor as a carried item, and the destination is fixed only when the player clicks a slot again. An empty destination moves the item, an occupied destination swaps it with the carry source, and a Creative All Items source replaces the destination. Closing the inventory while carrying returns the item to its source.

Shift and left click moves an item immediately through `place_into_storage_priority` and the per-region rules in `InventoryOverlay`: an All Items source fills the first empty hotbar slot and then the upper inventory, a hotbar item descends to the first empty upper slot, an upper item rises to the first empty hotbar slot, and a crafting slot returns to the hotbar and then the upper inventory.

Hovering an item and pressing `1` through `9` outside the search box assigns it to the matching hotbar slot. Creative Mode replaces the hotbar slot with the hovered item; Survival Mode swaps the hovered storage slot with the hotbar slot. The search field keeps `1` through `9` as text while it holds focus.

Pressing the drop key (default `Q`) while hovering a slot in the 9x4 storage empties that slot. The drop key acts on the hovered hotbar or upper slot, leaving the crafting and All Items regions untouched.

sections.title: Inventory Player Preview and Drag Image
items: Added a live player preview inside the inventory through `_update_inventory_preview_frame`, which composes a third-person preview state from the running render snapshot and reflects the current skin and hurt tint. The fixed-step runtime keeps advancing while the inventory stays open, so the preview tracks the player state in real time.

Scaled the drag image in `start_item_drag` down to the slot icon size with a centered hotspot, matching a block thumbnail to its in-slot appearance during a drag instead of the 300x300 thumbnail source.

sections.title: AI Death Logs
items: Added chat death-log rows for AI actors. Direct player kills now return `AiLocalAttackResult.target_death_log`, and fall, void, or generic AI deaths produced during `AiPlayerManager.step` now travel through `SessionStepResult.ai_death_logs` into the same runtime chat history used by local-player death messages.

Removed defeated AI actors immediately on direct player kills and continued cancelling their pending navigation plans, so the actor disappears from the simulation and the chat row records the terminal event without waiting for a later manager sweep.

sections.title: Chat Input and History Review
items: Finalized the Chat and Commands input boundary: clicks and wheel input inside the open chat surface no longer restore gameplay mouse capture, camera control, block interaction, hotbar selection, Othello input, or viewport focus.

Added a right-side history scrollbar, synchronized the message field with the settings and send controls at the bottom-bar height, restored the settings cog from `assets/ui/settings/cog.svg`, and aligned the Chat Settings Back control with the Send button family.

Added runtime-only sent-input recall for the focused message field. Up traverses the newest submitted messages and commands first; Down returns toward the current draft. Submitted validation-error commands remain recallable because the existing submission path accepts every nonempty command string before routing.

Added a thirty-second idle fade for the lower-left recent chat feed after the chat screen closes. The next display message restores the feed, and the existing F3 suppression and runtime history retention remain in force.

sections.title: Command Alias
items: Added `/tp` as an alias for `/teleport`, including command candidates. Both spellings share the same parser, validation, target resolution, coordinate handling, execution result, and command-error route.

sections.title: Chat and Commands Screen
items: Added a shared chat-and-commands screen for My World and Othello opened with the new `toggle_chat` keybind defaulting to `T`: `chat_controller.bind_chat` attaches a `ChatController` to both the OpenGL and WGPU viewport widgets, `interaction.handle_key_press` opens it through `ACTION_TOGGLE_CHAT`, and `Esc` or the title-bar `< Back` button closes it and restores gameplay capture for the active play space.

Kept the screen non-pausing: opening chat releases mouse capture and resets held input through `ViewportInput` without entering the dead, paused, settings, or transient-modal states, so `_tick_sim` and `_on_step` keep advancing the fixed-step runtime, the Othello clock, and cloud and AI motion while the input field holds focus; the screen background reuses the pause-screen `rgba(0,0,0,150)` fill without reusing the pause stop path.

Built the title bar and bottom bar as equal-height, full-width bars: the title bar carries a left `< Back` control, a fixed-width right balancing slot, and a stretched center label so `Chat and Commands` stays centered on the whole window width across resizes, and the bottom bar carries a 1:1 settings button, a stretched message field, and a 2:1 send button that submits on click or `Enter` while empty and whitespace-only input is dropped.

sections.title: Heads-Up Recent Chat Feed
items: Added a lower-left heads-up recent chat feed above the hotbar that shows the newest display messages after the chat screen closes: `ChatController.sync_visibility` shows it only while the gameplay HUD is active, the F3 Debug HUD is inactive, Mute All Chat is disabled, and the chat screen is closed, and `ChatFeedWidget` is transparent to mouse events so it never takes camera control, hotbar selection, or block interaction.

Suppressed the feed while the F3 Debug HUD is shown and restored it once the Debug HUD closes, the chat screen is closed, and Mute All Chat is disabled, limiting the box to the newest ten display rows while the runtime history retains up to one hundred messages.

sections.title: Section Formatting and Message Model
items: Added a Qt-free section-formatting contract under `src/ludoxel/foundations/text/`: `palette.py` holds the color table, `format_codes.py` parses `§` codes into style segments where a color code sets foreground and background and only `§r` clears the bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, and obfuscated flags, and `obfuscation.py` supplies same-width-class replacement characters for `§k` text.

Rendered chat text through the `ChatTextView` painter shared by the chat screen, the heads-up feed, command feedback, command errors, the periodic support message, and death-log rows, pinning each obfuscated glyph to the original character advance so cycling does not shift the layout, and limiting clickable external links to explicitly authored trusted spans.

sections.title: Chat Settings and Runtime History
items: Added an embedded Chat Settings surface opened from the bottom-bar settings button with the chat screen visible behind it; its single control is the runtime-only Mute All Chat toggle owned by the application `ChatRuntime`, held only for the running game and never written to saved preferences, the app-state schema, or any world or Othello save.

Kept the chat history runtime-only with a one-hundred-message cap in `ChatHistory`: messages always accumulate, Mute All Chat hides every kind in both the chat screen and the heads-up feed without deleting them, unmuting shows the retained messages again, and messages dropped by the cap are not restored.

Added a one-hundred-twenty-second support message that appends `§6[§e!§6] §7Project support: 5uog` to the history, where the `5uog` span is the only link and opens `https://github.com/5uog/` through the Qt desktop URL service while the rest of the message text carries no link.

sections.title: Teleport and Game Mode Commands
items: Added command candidate display and parsing under `src/ludoxel/application/chat/commands/`: a leading slash hides the message list and shows `/teleport` candidates for `/t` and `/gamemode` candidates for `/g`, an unknown prefix shows an empty candidate list rather than repeated errors, and the command coordinator routes execution through the simulation player operations.

Added `/teleport <x> <y> <z>` with an optional `chunkForBlocks` boolean, an optional `facing <x y z>` position, and an optional `facing <target>` entity: finite coordinates move the local player in My World and in the Othello play space, `teleport_player` zeroes velocity and resets fall-related player state, facing resolves a look direction through `yaw_pitch_deg_from_forward`, and a true `chunkForBlocks` arms a world-upload sync around the destination.

Added `/gamemode` accepting `survival`, `s`, `0`, `creative`, `c`, and `1` with an optional trailing player target resolved to the local player only, routed through the shared `apply_game_mode` operation that the Settings game-mode toggle now also uses.

Removed the `B` survival and creative toggle: the `toggle_creative_mode` keybind action is gone from the keybind catalog, defaults, display names, and the Controls tab, and game-mode changes now flow through the Settings surface and the `/gamemode` command.

sections.title: Debug HUD Axis Crosshair
items: Made the Debug HUD toggle swap the center crosshair for a world-axis crosshair: `_sync_gameplay_hud_visibility` calls `set_axis_crosshair_enabled(self._debug_hud_active())` on `CrosshairWidget`, so while the Debug HUD is active the widget paints three short arms for world `+X` in red, world `+Y` in green, and world `+Z` in blue, and the built-in or custom bitmap returns through the existing `set_pattern` path when the Debug HUD closes.

Projected the axis arms from the renderer effective camera every frame: the shared `paintGL` forwards `render_yaw_deg`, `render_pitch_deg`, and `render_roll_deg` to `set_axis_camera` for both the OpenGL and WGPU viewport widgets, and `axis_screen_offsets` resolves each world axis through the same look-direction basis and roll the world overlays use, so the arms turn with the camera and shorten as an axis rotates toward the view direction; a degenerate or non-finite axis is skipped to keep the drawn frame finite.

Kept the axis crosshair a transient diagnostic of the first-person gameplay HUD: it obeys the same visibility gate as the bitmap crosshair, draws its colors through `QPainter` pens instead of theme stylesheets, and leaves the saved `crosshair_mode` and `crosshair_pixels` and the Settings crosshair editor untouched.

sections.title: Player Attack Audio Mixer
items: Moved weak and strong attack one-shot playback off the `QSoundEffect` pool and into a bounded PCM mixer backed by `QAudioSink`, so rapid air-punch and attack samples overlap inside one continuous output stream instead of relying on multiple backend effect voices.

Kept material, landing, damage, Othello, and ambient audio on the existing playback paths; the mixer is limited to rapid player attack events and still obeys player volume, pool cooldown, sample selection, output-device refresh, and bounded voice count.

sections.title: Player Audio Overlap
items: Kept rapid player voices reserved for the measured WAV duration plus a small release pad, so a `QSoundEffect` slot is not considered reusable merely because Qt reports the queued effect as no longer playing before the audible tail has cleared.

Raised weak and strong attack swings to a twelve-voice bounded pool with no attack-event cooldown, preserving overlap for repeated air-punch and attack input while still dropping only when every reserved voice is busy.

sections.title: Audio Sample Voices
items: Allocated rapid one-shot player sounds across the whole event pool instead of a single randomly selected sample source: `_play_pool` now ensures the voice slots of every prepared source, gathers the sources that still hold an idle voice through `has_idle_voice`, and selects among only those, so a busy sample source no longer drops a request while other voices in the pool are idle.

Kept the pool bounded and overlap-only: when every voice in the pool is already playing, `_play_pool` drops the request rather than stopping an active voice, which lets repeated weak and strong attack swings overlap across their samples within the existing per-pool polyphony.

sections.title: Held Slab and Stair Placement
items: Fixed the first state of a held slab or stair bridge: when a placement extends from a slab or stair source into an adjacent empty cell through the support-face path, `resolve_place_state` now inherits the source slab `type`, or the source stair `facing` and `half`, through a new inherit-state context, so a lower-slab bridge starts as a lower slab and an upper-slab bridge starts as an upper slab even though the synthesized support-face hit point would otherwise read the opposite half.

Left ordinary single-click placement on hit geometry and same-cell opposite-half slab merging unchanged, and continued to lock the first committed state for the rest of the hold so the bridge keeps its slab type, or its stair facing and half, as the target cell advances and the camera turns.

sections.title: Audio Sample Voices
items: Stopped pooled sound effects from cutting an in-progress voice to replay the same sample: `next_effect_slot` now returns a loaded effect slot only when it is not already playing, and `_play_pool` no longer stops and restarts a playing slot, so a play request that finds every voice in a pool busy is dropped instead of truncating an audible sample.

Raised the weak attack-swing pool from two to eight voices so repeated swing-through-air sounds overlap across the four weak samples without falling back to dropped requests, while leaving the other player, block, surface, and ambient pool polyphony, cooldown, spatial cutoff, and volume categories unchanged.

sections.title: Fall Damage Audio
items: Counted fall damage when deciding whether to play the damage sound: the session step now reports `play_damage_sound` for any fall damage past the safe distance, not only void and combat damage.

Added a `play_landing_sound` field to the session step result and suppressed the landing sound on a step that applied fall damage, so a damaging landing plays the damage hit while a non-damaging landing still plays its surface landing sample.

sections.title: Structural Hull Collision
items: Resolved each horizontal collision axis against every overlapping box: `_axis_collision_position` now clamps the player to the nearest blocking face across all intersecting boxes and re-tests with the updated box until it is clear, replacing the single-pass resolution that could leave the player inside the tall structural hull of a fence, wall, or closed fence gate.

Added a final depenetration pass after the X, Y, and Z moves in `integrate_with_collisions`, pushing a player that would otherwise remain inside a collision box back out before the position is committed, zeroing the corrected velocity components and treating an upward correction as ground contact.

sections.title: Held Fence Gate Placement
items: Made the right-click placement repeat prefer interaction for a held fence gate: when the held block is a fence gate, the player is not crouching, and the current target is a fence gate, the repeat toggles that gate and stops rather than continuing to place gates in the adjacent cells, while a crouching hold still places gates and single placement is unchanged.

sections.title: Held Slab and Stair Placement
items: Locked the resolved block state of a held placement repeat to its first committed result: the repeat reuses the initial slab type and the initial stair facing and half (and fence gate facing) for the rest of the hold by threading a forced place state through `place_block_from_hit`, so changing aim no longer flips slabs between top and bottom or rotates stairs mid-hold.

Kept the placement target cell advancing during the locked hold and limited same-slab opposite-half merging to the locked type, and released the lock when the selected hotbar item changes or the right mouse button is released.

sections.title: Dynamic Face Upload
items: Stopped the shared textured face pass from reusing a previous frame’s GPU instance buffer when falling blocks, first-person held blocks, arms, special items, block-break particles, player skins, or player-held blocks rebuild their per-face transform rows with the same row count, by removing the object-identity and row-count upload-skip condition so every non-empty face uploads the current transform and UV rows before drawing.
Applied the same per-frame upload to the player-model shadow pass so the ground shadow uploads the current instance rows rather than caching them by object identity.

sections.title: Windows Audio Device Recovery
items: Rebound pooled sound effects and the ambient effect to the current default audio output when Windows reports an output-device change, preventing stale WASAPI streams from continuing after the endpoint is invalidated.
